_readme: TEMPLATE for devices.json: every section the config supports, in one file. Copy what you need; the service
never reads this file. Smaller per-type starting points are in examples/. Save devices.json to reload it.
"profiles": define a NEW device type in JSON, no Python (here a CO2 sensor): data_ports, fields (codec field
-> measurement, with calibration such as $co2_scale), rules (alarm when a value passes a limit) and the
type's own defaults. The built-in types (one file each in loralarm/families/)
need no entry.
"defaults": applies to every device. Secrets are ${ENV_VAR} placeholders, set once here (Pushover) so no
device needs its own copy. "timezone" (default Europe/Stockholm) is used by alarm_window.
alarm_window: "HH:MM-HH:MM" (overnight ok, e.g. Door2 21:00-09:00 = door alarms only at night). Outside it the
alarm is NOT sent but still logged. Temperature, battery and no-contact alarms ignore it; list exact kinds
with "alarm_window_kinds" to change that. See README "Alarm window".
"families": applies to every device of one type (key = ChirpStack device-profile name, exact spelling).
"devices": one entry per sensor, keyed by lowercase devEUI. Only name and family are required.
Precedence, later wins: the type's built-in defaults, defaults, families, the device entry. "params" merge
key by key; a dict such as notify_fire is replaced as a whole by the more specific layer.
application_id is set per device (not in a shared layer): devices of one type can use different applications.
"web_users": PWA accounts for --web (invite tokens, stored hashed in SQLite; seeded at startup and on every
reload — removing a user disables them immediately). role "admin" may also disarm a device "tills vidare";
everyone else gets snooze presets (1/8/24 h). Tokens are ${ENV_VAR} placeholders, never literal secrets.
Device visibility: "group" on a device + "groups" on a web_user decide who sees it in the PWA (and gets its
pushes). Groups only affect role "user": an admin ALWAYS sees every device, grouped or not — a "groups"
key on an admin is ignored, so omit it. A device WITHOUT a group is visible to every user (so a new device
can never alarm to nobody). If non-admins must only see their own devices, give EVERY device a group.
Several recipients per device are not available yet (planned).
PWA Web Push (VAPID) is NOT configured here: one keypair per server, a secret like Pushover — set
LORALARM_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY (+ LORALARM_VAPID_SUB) in the env file; users subscribe in the PWA.
Temperature alarms: temp_alarm_min_c (alarm at or below), temp_alarm_max_c (alarm at or above; unset = off),
temp_alarm_hysteresis_c (applies to both limits: the alarm clears only this many degrees back inside the limit).
